projectCards.title: Jade Pruning Project
projectCards.description: The family jade story, the actual mother plant before and after the June 29 pruning, and the cuttings and pups being raised to share.

projectCards.title: Haworthia & Pups
projectCards.description: A corrected photo timeline from the crowded mother plant through separation and repotting.

projectCards.title: Eagle Tree Carving
projectCards.description: Four documented carving days of Dan Burns transforming the preserved tree into a bald eagle and woodland-wildlife sculpture. Day 4 is included, and the project remains in progress.
projectCards.alt: Day 4 eagle tree carving overlooking the lake

projectCards.title: Tree Removal – Poulin Tree
projectCards.description: The original tree, bucket-truck work, limb removal, and preparation of the tall trunk for the carving.

projectCards.title: Grape Arbor Improvement
projectCards.description: A photo-based pruning and training plan to open the canopy, improve airflow, and produce larger, sweeter grape crops without rebuilding the arbor.

journalEntries.title: Squash & Pumpkin Bed Check
journalEntries.summary: Widespread yellowing was recorded while vines continued flowering and setting fruit. Flower-tone had been applied about three weeks earlier. Soil moisture, nutrient demand, and magnesium uptake will be checked before additional feeding.
journalEntries.alt: Squash and pumpkin vines with widespread pale foliage

journalEntries.title: Epsom Salt Applied to Vine Crops
journalEntries.summary: Pumpkins, squash, and cucumbers received one tablespoon of Epsom salt per gallon of water. The solution was applied at the plant bases without wetting the leaves.
journalEntries.keywords: epsom salt pumpkin squash cucumber magnesium milk jug base watering

journalEntries.title: Flower-tone for Vine Crops
journalEntries.summary: Planned application for pumpkins, winter squash, summer squash, and cucumbers. Apply around the drip line, keep fertilizer away from stems, and water it in thoroughly.
journalEntries.alt: Vine crops growing in the vegetable garden
journalEntries.keywords: flower tone fertilizer pumpkin squash cucumber schedule

journalEntries.title: Garlic Harvest & Curing
journalEntries.summary: Garlic was harvested and placed in a shaded, airy location to cure for roughly two to four weeks.

journalEntries.title: Detroit Beet Harvest
journalEntries.summary: Detroit beets were checked and the largest roots harvested first. Remaining plants should stay evenly moist.

journalEntries.title: Blueberry Crop Update
journalEntries.summary: Blueberry bushes showed a heavy crop with ripe and ripening fruit. Continue harvesting every two to three days and maintain bird protection.

journalEntries.title: Blueberry Propagation
journalEntries.summary: Cuttings remain under humidity domes with green stems and firm leaves. Keep in bright indirect light and vent slightly if condensation is excessive.
journalEntries.keywords: blueberry cuttings humidity dome heat mat roots propagation project

journalEntries.title: Zebra Haworthia Pup Project
journalEntries.summary: The mother plant was divided, pups were separated, and the new plants were potted individually.

journalEntries.title: Jade Pruning Project
journalEntries.summary: The family mother jade was pruned to encourage branching. Monthly photographs will be used to compare new growth and follow the saved cuttings.

journalEntries.title: Bees & Garden Pollination
journalEntries.summary: Close-up photographs show bees working squash blossoms, including a bee covered in yellow pollen.
journalEntries.alt: Pollen-covered bee in a squash blossom

journalEntries.title: Woodland Habitat Carving · Day 4
journalEntries.summary: Day 4 added more feather, fur, and wildlife detail. The carving remains in progress, with finishing and additional refinement still to come.
